He played [[college basketball]] for [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]] before being selected with the 41st overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]] by the [[Orlando Magic]]. ==High school career== [[File:20150401 MCDAAG Stephen Zimmerman from up close (2).JPG |thumb|left|upright|Zimerman in the [[2015 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2015 McDonald's All-American Game]]]] Zimmerman attended [[Bishop Gorman High School]] in [[Las Vegas]], Nevada, where he led the Gaels to four straight state championships, becoming the only player in Nevada history to accomplish the feat at the large-school level. His 114 career wins also made him the winningest player in school history. As a senior in 2014–15, Zimmerman averaged 14.7 points, 10.1 rebounds, 4.2 assists, 1.2 steals and 2.4 blocks per game. He subsequently earned selection to the [[2015 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]] and the [[Jordan Brand Classic]].{{cite web |title=Stephen Zimmerman Jr. Bio |url=https://unlvrebels.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/stephen-jr-/5221 |accessdate=August 7, 2023 |work=UNLVRebels.com}} ==College career== Zimmerman played one season of college basketball for [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]]. As a freshman in [[2015–16 UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball team|2015–16]], he played in 26 games, made 24 starts, and averaged 10.5 points, a team-high 8.7 rebounds and a team-high 1.96 blocks in 26.2 minutes per game. He ranked second in the [[Mountain West Conference]] in blocked shots and third in rebounding. He scored in double figures 17 times, including a career-high 21 points on February 2 against [[2015–16 New Mexico Lobos men's basketball team|New Mexico]]. Zimmerman pulled down double-figure rebounds 13 times, including a career-best 16 boards on January 19 against [[2015–16 Utah State Aggies men's basketball team|Utah State]].{{cite web |last=Cohen |first=Josh |date=July 7, 2016 |title=Orlando Magic Sign Stephen Zimmerman |url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-sign-stephen-zimmerman |accessdate=July 7, 2016 |work=NBA.com}} On March 28, 2016, Zimmerman declared for the [[2016 NBA draft|NBA draft]], forgoing his final three years of college eligibility.{{cite web|first=Mark|last=Anderson|url=http://www.reviewjournal.com/sports/unlv-rebels/basketball/stephen-zimmerman-jr-officially-announces-he-will-enter-nba-draft|title=Stephen Zimmerman Jr. officially announces he will enter NBA Draft|work=ReviewJournal.com|date=March 28, 2016|accessdate=July 7, 2016}} ==Professional career== ===Orlando Magic (2016–2017)=== On June 23, 2016, Zimmerman was selected by the [[Orlando Magic]] with the 41st overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]].{{cite web |last=Savage |first=Dan |date=June 23, 2016 |title=Magic Select Stephen Zimmerman 41st Overall in NBA Draft |url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-select-stephen-zimmerman-41st-overall-nba-draft/ |accessdate=July 7, 2016 |work=NBA.com}} On July 7, 2016, he signed with the Magic. During his rookie season, Zimmerman had multiple assignments with the [[Osceola Magic|Erie BayHawks]], the Magic's [[D-League]] affiliate.{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2016-17 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|accessdate=December 31, 2016|archive-date=January 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170126075350/http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|url-status=dead}} He also played in 19 games with Orlando, averaging 1.2 points, 1.8 rebounds and 5.7 minutes per game.{{cite web |last=Cohen |first=Josh |date=July 4, 2017 |title=Magic Waive Stephen Zimmerman |url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-waive-stephen-zimmerman |accessdate=July 4, 2017 |work=NBA.com}} On July 4, 2017, Zimmerman was waived by the Magic. ===South Bay Lakers (2017–2018)=== On August 9, 2017, Zimmerman signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers sign center Stephen Zimmerman|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/08/09/los-angeles-lakers-sign-stephen-zimmerman|website=NBA.com|date=August 9, 2017|accessdate=August 9, 2017|language=en}} On October 9, 2017, he was waived by the Lakers.{{cite web |date=October 9, 2017 |title=Stephen Zimmerman: Waived by Lakers
